title: Edge-Deployed Logistics Assistant
business: Logistics firms managing remote warehouse operations with limited connectivity.
problem: High latency and data privacy concerns when sending sensitive inventory manifests to cloud-based APIs for parsing.
solution: Deploying the Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model locally on edge hardware to process structured inventory data and generate natural language summaries without external network dependencies.
steps: Install the latest transformers library to ensure compatibility with the Qwen2.5 architecture.
Load the model using AutoModelForCausalLM with device_map set to auto for hardware optimization.
Initialize the tokenizer and apply the chat template to format system and user instructions.
Pass the inventory manifest as a user message to the model for structured output generation.
Decode the generated tokens into a readable summary for warehouse staff.
outcome: Improved operational autonomy and reduced data exposure by keeping all inventory processing within the local network.
limitation: The 1.5B parameter size is optimized for efficiency but may struggle with highly complex, multi-step reasoning compared to larger models; verify performance by testing against diverse, edge-case inventory queries.

nodes.label: Tokenizer
nodes.detail: Applies chat template to raw data

code.content:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
# Load model locally
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct", device_map="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct")
# Prepare input with chat template
messages = [{"role": "system", "content": "Summarize the inventory."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Manifest: 50 units SKU-A"}]
text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
inputs = tokenizer([text], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
# Generate response
generated = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=100)
